log:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert — sudden KV cache footprint surge and paging on inference fleet in us-west-2. Elevated 95/99 p90 latency and OOM-ish eviction churn. auto-triage: possible correlation with last night’s quant/kernel rollout to awq-int8 variant.

alex: seeing it on dashboards too. p95 gen latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.8s for a subset of routes. paging reads/sec up ~10x, disk IO saturated on multiple pods. :eyes:

devon: root cause hypothesis: AWQ int8 kernel increases KV cache per-entry size due to different kv layout + kernel selection fallback causing duplicate caches. Combined with continuous batching config (max_batch_tokens=2048) we might be retaining much bigger KV for long-lived sessions.

lily: customers affected: heavy-chat customers and a few dedicated tenants. AcmeCorp reported timeouts. Revenue-impacting? small fraction but replicated across many routes so tail latencies rising. 

anya: error rate spike: 0.4% -> 2.7% 5xxs on text-generation endpoints. Autoscale partially absorbing traffic but paging is increasing cost and causing extra latency.

alex: can we get a quick snapshot of KV sizes by model and quant path? running query on telemetry now.

eng_oncall: paste of telemetry snippet: 
```
model  awq-int8   avg_kv_bytes  ->  3.2MB (baseline fp16: 0.9MB)
model  gptq-4bit  avg_kv_bytes  ->  1.1MB
overall cache_entries   ->  +420% vs yesterday
disk paging rate -> 5.3k/sec (baseline 420/sec)
```

devon: that matches my local reproducer — AWQ int8 currently stores kv as 32-bit aligned blocks due to kernel layout, so footprint ~3-4x.

opsbot: deploy-bot: `deploy/infra/quant-kernel/awq-int8` rolled out 2026-03-14T02:12Z to us-west-2

lily: immediate mitigations we can try in parallel:
- rollback awq-int8 kernel to previous kernel variant on affected nodes (fast)
- lower continuous batching max_batch_tokens / increase batch timeout to force smaller kv lifetimes
- reduce per-pod kv_cache_max_entries temporarily
- route traffic away from affected capacity to fallback region (canary only)

alex: I'll prepare a rollback. devon, can you test a quick config change: set kv_cache_max_entries=500 and batch.max_tokens=1024 on a small subset? want to see if eviction stabilizes.

devon: doing that now on canary pool id=c-cache-02. will watch evictions and p95.

[5m later]

devon: canary results: evictions dropped 72%, p95 down to ~300ms (from 1.8s), paging rate down to 900/sec. Looks promising.

lily: recommend full rollback of awq-int8 on all serving nodes in us-west-2 and apply temporary kv_cache_max_entries=800 cluster-wide until we fix kernel.

anya: notifying impacted customers now. pinged AcmeCorp support and put status update on status.redwood.example.

pagerduty: @pagerduty incident assigned to eng-sre oncall — high severity.

eng_oncall: initiating rollback now. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference set image ds/quant-kernel quant-kernel=quant-kernel:v2026.03.13-prev --selector=region=us-west-2
```

opsbot: rolling restart triggered. patch applied to 12/24 pods so far. expected 8m to complete.

[10m later]

alex: rollback completed across us-west-2. metrics slowly normalizing. p95 at 160ms, paging back to baseline, evictions normalized.

devon: rolling back also restored previous kernel selection path; need to investigate why awq-int8 caused duplicate cache allocations when certain kernels fallback to host path. likely a kernel metadata mismatch bug.

lily: status update for customers: "Mitigated — rollback of recent quant/kernel change. We’re performing a deep postmortem and will follow up with timeline and remediation steps." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: SEV2 -> Mitigated. Moving to monitoring mode. :white_check_mark:

alex: handoff: i'm off in 25m. lily, can you take primary for postmortem + customer comms? I'll add notes to incident doc.

lily: taking handoff. I'll open postmortem draft and assign follow-ups. immediate action items:
- add regression test for kv footprint across quant paths (int8/awq/gptq) with realistic prompts
- add telemetry alert for sudden avg_kv_bytes increase (>2x baseline)
- add canary gate for kernel rollouts that measures KV footprint on canary nodes before full rollout
- consider adding memory-friendly kernel path that enforces 4bit packing for kv

anya: also add a runbook tweak: when paging spike + eviction churn, prefer kernel rollback + tighten batch config as first steps.

devon: i'm going to reproduce kernel layout discrepancy locally and submit a PR to kernel selection to avoid duplicate allocations. will include instrumented flags.

alex: quick note — we saw continuous batching config amplified the issue. longer-lived large batches kept larger kvs resident. we should consider defaults that cap per-session kv retention when using aggressive quant paths.

lily: agreed. final notes: incident duration ~1h 30m. impacted routes ~8% of production traffic, primary cause: AWQ-int8 kernel rollout caused KV footprint increase x3 on that quant path combined with continuous batching config leading to paging and evictions. Mitigation: rollback kernel + temporary kv/batch config adjustments. Next: postmortem, tests, canary gating, and customer follow-up.

eng_oncall: handing off to lily for postmortem. tagging participants for follow-up: @devon @alex @anya @opsbot

lily: acknowledged. I'll prepare postmortem doc and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to go over fixes. :calendar: 

end-of-thread-bot: thread closed for updates; reopen if metrics flare.
